clue.text: Isolated device for stopping flow

definitions.meaning: a place ... is isolated, separated from everything around it
a valve or switch that shuts off a supply of water, gas or current

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: as a phrasal verb it means separated, as a noun it is a shut-off valve.

clue.text: Match clash

definitions.meaning: events clash when they fall at the same time

explanation.definitionFit: It means both to correspond and, of events, to happen simultaneously.

clue.text: Frantic hustle about university with a drink habitually ordered

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the next pieces
frantic suggests the letters are thrown about wildly

explanation.surface: A frantic rush around campus with someone's regular order at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frantic' rearranges HUSTLE into THESL, and 'about' wraps it round U and A after THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular at a pub asks for their customary drink with this phrase.

clue.text: Jack regarding the bottle

parts.note: a jack is a flag flown on a ship
on means about or regarding

explanation.surface: A man named Jack thinking about the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a name; it is a ship's flag, as in Union Jack.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large bottle or jug for wine or cider.

clue.text: Guesswork promises could be misleading

parts.note: spec, short for speculation, is a venture on guesswork
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: Promises built on guesswork may turn out to be deceptive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On spec' means on a speculative basis; IOU stands for 'I owe you', a written promise of payment. 'could be' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A specious argument looks plausible but is in fact false, so it is misleading.

clue.text: Look up and down

indicators.note: the word reads the same whether read up or down the grid

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Glance upward and downward.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the word reads the same bottom to top as top to bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick peek is a brief look.

clue.text: Double feature of good health

indicators.note: double means the word appears twice in a row

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A double chin is a feature of a well-fed person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double feature' evokes cinema and double chins; the answer is a toast like 'Cheers!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking toast wishing health, like 'Cheers!'.

clue.text: Made speech to read when relaxing

indicators.note: relaxing loosens the letters so they can settle in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone gave a talk, reading out to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relaxing' rearranges TO READ; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal address.

clue.text: Gardens in the south-east with river to run through

indicators.note: the gardens sit inside the letters for south-east

parts.note: SE is the abbreviation for south-east
Kew Gardens is the botanical garden in London

explanation.surface: Gardens in south-east England where a river runs through.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW, the Royal Botanic Gardens in south-west London, goes inside SE, then R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce something with a spit or pin is to run it through.

clue.text: Freezing point?

parts.note: not a temperature but a point, a summit or pole, covered by permanent frozen sheet

explanation.definitionFit: The polar ice sheet sits at the top of the globe, a frozen peak.

clue.text: Delay as the tie is done up

indicators.note: the letters are fixed up into a new arrangement, the way a tie is done up

explanation.surface: Someone is held back while fussing over knotting their necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done up' fits the tie in the surface but is the anagram signal on AS THE TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pause or hold back from acting is to delay.

clue.text: A governor with money on the list coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue the coin sits on top of the next piece

parts.note: a sen is a small coin of Japan and other Asian countries

indicators.note: in a down clue the list is read upwards

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties

explanation.surface: A governor with cash is on the duty list going up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns ROTA into ATOR beneath SEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a ruling council, one who governs.

clue.text: They say one's never wrong

parts.note: refers to the shop saying that the person buying is always right

explanation.definitionFit: The retail slogan holds that a shopper is always right.

clue.text: Consent to month returns in first class

indicators.note: the turned month goes inside the term for first class

parts.note: an ace is something first-rate

indicators.note: the month's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to a month coming back in a top-grade fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns DEC into CED, which 'in' places inside ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree to a request or demand is to give consent.

clue.text: Fellow feeling power?

parts.note: the capacity to share what a fellow being feels, read as a kind of power

explanation.definitionFit: Sympathetic understanding of another's emotions is fellow feeling.

clue.text: Have business relations with board

definitions.meaning: to trade with or handle someone commercially
a plank of pine or fir timber

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb with 'with' it means trade with; as a noun it is softwood planking.

clue.text: She provides assistance with the froth

parts.note: barm is the froth on fermenting malt liquor
aid means help

explanation.surface: A woman who helps out with the head on a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: BARM is the yeasty froth on brewing beer; 'provides' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The woman serving drinks in a pub is referred to by 'She'.

clue.text: Man's record about the conflict an illusion

parts.note: Tim is a man's name

indicators.note: the record goes around the conflict

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
war is conflict

explanation.surface: A man's record of a war is a fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts WAR inside EP, after TIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A distortion in which time seems to slip is a kind of illusion.

clue.text: Worship Old Testament one in the county

indicators.note: the next pieces are placed inside the county

parts.note: Devon is a county in south-west England
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Worship of the Old Testament in a county church.
explanation.walkthrough: DEVON is a county in south-west England; 'in' places OT and I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious devotion is reverent worship.

clue.text: Troubled the old collecting one heap of shoddy stuff

indicators.note: the old word gathers the next pieces inside it

parts.note: aged means old
I is the Roman numeral for one
tat is cheap shoddy goods

explanation.surface: An elderly person is upset at gathering a pile of junk.
explanation.walkthrough: TAT is British slang for tasteless junk; 'collecting' puts I and TAT inside AGED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone agitated is anxious and troubled.

clue.text: Sea mass to which bird in the main returns

indicators.note: the shortened bird is read backwards
in the main means mostly, so the bird loses its last letter

parts.note: a grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: A floating mass at sea that a seabird keeps coming back to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' (mostly) cuts GREBE to GREB; 'returns' turns that into the answer. 'the main' also means the sea, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An iceberg is a huge floating mass of ice in the sea.

clue.text: Band of singers in part echo RU songs

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A choir singing part of some echoing Russian songs.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is an organised group of singers.

clue.text: British game thats not with it

parts.note: lotto is a game of chance like bingo

explanation.surface: A British game is not for those who are with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not with it' means in no fit state; the answer is British slang for very drunk. 'thats' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone very drunk is dazed and not alert.

clue.text: Was the working a bind ?

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are worked into another order

explanation.surface: Was the work a nuisance?
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bind' looks like a nuisance; it is a band of cloth that binds or wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: A swathe is a strip of fabric used to wrap or bind.

clue.text: Protective wear when making the move around tree

indicators.note: the shuffled letters surround the tree
making the word move rearranges its letters

parts.note: an elm is a tree

explanation.surface: Someone puts on safety gear before shifting about a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' turns THE into HET, which goes 'around' ELM.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard hat is headgear worn for protection.

clue.text: Musical vessel on display

indicators.note: the vessel is placed on the end of the display

parts.note: a show is a display
a boat is a vessel

explanation.surface: A singing boat is put on show.
explanation.walkthrough: Show Boat is the 1927 Kern and Hammerstein musical about a Mississippi riverboat.
explanation.definitionFit: Show Boat is a famous American stage musical.

clue.text: Slight noise of drink not quiet

indicators.note: not means the letter for quiet is left out

parts.note: a slurp is the noise of noisy drinking
p, piano, is the musical term for quiet

explanation.surface: A small sound made while drinking, but not quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes P, the musical abbreviation for quiet, from SLURP.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur is an insult, a slight on someone's name.

clue.text: Fuzzy, blear, taking in drink that can be assessed

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold the drink inside them
fuzzy suggests a blurred, jumbled version of the letters

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: Bleary eyes and a cuppa, in a judgement on what can be valued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fuzzy' rearranges BLEAR to RABLE, and 'taking in' puts TEA after its RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something whose value can be fixed or rated for tax is assessable.

clue.text: Enforced rigidly in restriction

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A rule applied rigidly as a restriction.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe rule is one applied rigidly without exception.

clue.text: Playwright's to finish page with notice about right

parts.note: to stop is to finish

indicators.note: the notice goes round the letter for right

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper

explanation.surface: A dramatist is told to wrap up the page with a notice about the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside AD. Tom Stoppard is the British playwright of Arcadia and Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Stoppard is a leading British writer of plays.

clue.text: By means of a head movement the aperitif appears

parts.note: per means by means of, as in per post
a nod is a movement of the head

explanation.surface: A drink appears when someone nods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pernod is a French anise-flavoured spirit drunk before meals.
